title: Saudi Green Falcons Face Ecuador Friendly in New Jersey as World Cup Preparation Begins
detail: The Saudi national football team (the Green Falcons) played a pre-tournament friendly against Ecuador on May 30 in Harrison, New Jersey, as part of their World Cup 2026 preparation camp based in New York City. The team had departed Riyadh on May 25 following the announcement of the preliminary 30-man squad by Greek coach Georgios Donis. Saudi Arabia is drawn in Group A for the 2026 FIFA World Cup alongside host nation United States, Mexico, and Uruguay — considered a challenging group that will test the Kingdom's football program against established continental powers. The preparations represent a strategic moment for Saudi football: MBS has reoriented the PIF's sports portfolio away from LIV Golf and toward football infrastructure, with Saudi Arabia hosting the 2034 FIFA World Cup requiring substantial domestic stadiums, training facilities, and football development programs. The Green Falcons' performance in 2026 will directly influence global perception of Saudi Arabia's readiness as a hosting nation.

media.caption: Saudi Arabia's Green Falcons begin World Cup 2026 preparation in New Jersey

title: Hajj 2026 Concludes Successfully with 1.7 Million Pilgrims Under Saudi Custodianship
detail: Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Interior announced the successful conclusion of Hajj 2026 (1447 AH) on May 30, with approximately 1.7 million pilgrims completing the pilgrimage — 1,546,655 from abroad and 160,646 domestic pilgrims. The Hajj had proceeded without the large-scale security incidents that marred events in 1987, 1997, or 2015. Saudi Arabia's role as Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques — a title held by King Salman and central to the monarchy's legitimacy — underpinned the smooth management of the world's largest annual gathering of Muslims. The Kingdom managed the 2026 Hajj under exceptional circumstances: the Iran war and Hormuz closure had created regional instability, but Saudi Arabia maintained logistical access for pilgrims from across the Muslim world. A separate announcement confirmed plans for a new airport and metro system in Makkah ahead of future Hajj seasons, consistent with Vision 2030 infrastructure targets.

media.caption: Hajj 2026 concludes with 1.7M pilgrims; Saudi Arabia announces new Makkah airport and metro plans
